question: In what year was the historic Alma-Ata Declaration on Primary Health Care adopted?
explanation: The landmark international conference that defined Primary Health Care took place in Alma-Ata in 1978. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is the primary focus of Primary Health Care compared to tertiary hospital care?

options.A: Community-level prevention and basic health promotion
options.B: Providing exclusive care for wealthy urban citizens
options.C: Advanced surgical procedures and organ transplants
options.D: Managing rare and complicated genetic diseases

explanation: Primary Health Care brings essential, everyday health services and disease prevention directly into local communities. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is the most effective way for a nurse to communicate health education in a rural Nigerian community?

options.B: Using simple local languages and clear pictures
options.D: Speaking only in technical medical English

explanation: To ensure understanding, health education must be delivered in a language and format that everyday community members easily grasp. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h2)

question: A nurse wants to teach mothers how to prevent severe dehydration from watery stools in infants. What should be the main demonstration?

options.A: How to mix and give oral rehydration salt solution
options.B: How to isolate the child in a dark room
options.C: How to completely stop the baby from drinking fluids
options.D: How to perform emergency intravenous surgery

explanation: Teaching mothers home preparation of oral rehydration solution saves lives by treating early fluid loss before it becomes critical. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why is proper nutrition considered a core element of Primary Health Care?

options.A: Nutrition is only important for professional athletes
options.B: Good nutrition strengthens immunity and prevents infectious diseases
options.C: Eating expensive foreign food cures chronic illnesses
options.D: Food supply is managed strictly by the federal military

explanation: Well-nourished bodies fight off infections much more effectively, reducing the burden of disease in the community. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h3)

question: What simple tool do nurses use at local health clinics to catch early signs of poor growth in infants?
explanation: Regular weighing and plotting on growth charts help nurses spot faltering nutrition before severe malnutrition sets in. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which of the following is a simple, effective home method to make unsafe drinking water safer?

options.A: Adding heavy machine oil to the bucket
options.C: Leaving the water uncovered in the sun
options.D: Stirring the water with a dirty stick

explanation: Boiling kills harmful bacteria, viruses, and parasites present in untreated water sources. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why must pit latrines be constructed a safe distance away from community drinking wells?

options.A: To prevent underground waste seepage from contaminating the drinking water
options.B: To ensure the toilets receive enough direct sunlight
options.C: To keep the water source smelling fresh and perfumed
options.D: To make it harder for children to play near the toilets

explanation: Locating latrines too close to water wells allows sewage to leak into the groundwater, causing widespread water-borne outbreaks. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is a major goal of family planning within Primary Health Care?

options.A: Helping parents properly space their children for better health
options.B: Controlling the exact height of newborn babies
options.C: Ensuring families only have male children
options.D: Completely banning families from having children

explanation: Family planning allows mothers to regain their health between pregnancies and ensures better care for existing children. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h5)

question: A pregnant woman visits a primary health clinic for her first antenatal checkup. Which intervention should the nurse prioritize to prevent a deadly newborn infection?

options.A: Providing a prescription for high-dose sleeping pills
options.C: Fitting the patient with thick prescription eyeglasses

explanation: Tetanus toxoid given during pregnancy protects both the mother and the newborn from neonatal tetanus. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h5)

question: How do vaccines primarily protect the human body from infectious diseases?

options.A: By training the immune system to fight specific germs safely
options.B: By washing away germs with hot soapy water
options.C: By completely blocking the sense of taste
options.D: By permanently changing the person's blood type

explanation: Vaccines introduce weakened or killed parts of a germ so the immune system learns to recognize and defeat it later. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h6)

question: Why is maintaining the cold chain critical when storing and transporting vaccines in rural clinics?

options.A: It prevents the vaccine bottles from freezing into solid ice
options.B: It keeps vaccines potent and effective against disease
options.C: It allows the nurse to see the vaccine labels clearly
options.D: It makes the liquid vaccines taste better for babies

explanation: Most vaccines are sensitive to heat; if the cold chain breaks, the vaccines spoil and fail to protect the child. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h6)

question: What is an endemic disease?

options.A: A rare disease that only appears once every century
options.B: A physical injury resulting from a motor vehicle accident
options.C: A medical condition caused entirely by eating too much sugar
options.D: An infection that is constantly present within a specific region

explanation: Endemic diseases, such as malaria in tropical climates, maintain a steady presence in the local area. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h7)

question: Why is Directly Observed Therapy (DOT) used for treating patients with tuberculosis?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of hospital building construction
options.B: To punish patients who forget to visit the clinic on time
options.C: To ensure patients take every dose correctly and prevent drug resistance
options.D: To make the tuberculosis bacteria grow faster in the lungs

explanation: Watching patients take their medication guarantees adherence, which stops dangerous drug-resistant strains of tuberculosis from emerging. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of treating common diseases and minor injuries at a primary health center?

options.A: To practice advanced brain surgery on everyday patients
options.B: To keep patients admitted in bed for several weeks
options.C: To resolve health problems early and prevent dangerous complications
options.D: To replace all major regional hospitals in the country

explanation: Treating simple ailments promptly stops them from worsening into severe medical emergencies. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h8)

question: A patient arrives at a local primary health clinic with a deep, bleeding wound and signs of shock. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Prescribe mild herbal tea and send the patient away
options.B: Provide first aid, stabilize the wound, and arrange urgent referral to a hospital
options.C: Tell the patient to walk home and rest quietly in bed
options.D: Wait until the next national health campaign day to treat them

explanation: Severe injuries and shock exceed primary clinic capabilities, requiring immediate stabilization and referral to a higher level of care. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h8)

question: What does the term 'essential drugs' refer to in Primary Health Care?

options.A: Rare experimental drugs tested only on laboratory animals
options.B: Expensive imported cosmetics sold at private pharmacies
options.C: Life-saving medicines that satisfy the priority health needs of the population
options.D: Traditional herbs harvested secretly at midnight

explanation: Essential drugs are selected based on public health relevance, safety, and cost-effectiveness to treat common conditions. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h9)

question: Why must nurses regularly check the expiration dates of medicines in a clinic pharmacy?

options.A: To decide which nurse gets a promotion
options.B: To prevent patients from receiving expired or ineffective drugs
options.C: To make the medicine shelves look neat and colorful
options.D: To increase the financial profit of the local government

explanation: Expired medications may lose their chemical potency or become toxic, harming the patient instead of curing them. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h9)

question: Why is community engagement a crucial part of a nurse's role in implementing PHC in Nigeria?

options.A: It prevents nurses from having to work inside physical clinic buildings
options.B: It forces villagers to obey nursing orders without asking questions
options.C: It ensures health programs are culturally accepted and supported by local leaders
options.D: It eliminates the need for any government funding or medical supplies

explanation: When local leaders and community members are involved, they embrace health initiatives, leading to long-term success. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h10)

question: Which of the following best describes the multi-faceted role of a nurse working in a Nigerian primary health center?

options.A: Acting as a clinician, educator, manager, and community advocate
options.B: Writing laws and policies for the federal parliament
options.C: Performing complex heart surgeries in a private luxury suite
options.D: Working strictly as an accountant in a corporate bank office

explanation: PHC nurses handle diverse responsibilities, from treating patients and teaching families to managing clinic supplies and leading community health outreach. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h10)
